messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: High GPU queue depth observed in us-west-2 serving pool (severity: P1) — threshold breached 3m ago. cc @liv (oncall) link: https://metrics.redwood/alert/1968887777 :rotating_light:
liv (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing dashboards. who has the timeline of first signs?
matt: I saw elevated 95th latency at 09:21 UTC, request queue started rising around 09:18. customer-facing errors minimal so far, but token lag spikes.
sana: tagging failures: warmup_driver timed out a few times in the logs. suspect warmup delays causing capacity to lag behind HPA.
kevin: sharing quick snippets — from worker logs around 09:19:
```
2026-03-15T09:18:59Z WARN warmup_driver: kernel_warmup timeout=12000ms pool=pool-gpu-3 id=drv-7
2026-03-15T09:19:04Z INFO queue: enqueued=312 drain_rate=20 target_capacity=4
2026-03-15T09:19:30Z ERROR runtime: OOM while allocating kv_cache shard=5
```
tilly (infra): HPA events look fine, it issued scale-up from 4->6 at 09:20 but nodes not ready until 09:26 according to cloud events. kube events: `PodPending` due to image pull + gpu plugin init.
liv (oncall): customer-impact? cust-success-bot, do we have open tickets?
cust-success-bot: Notified top 5 customers via status page; two reported elevated latency in the last 10m, no errors reported yet.
matt: current queue depth snapshot at 09:28: `queue_depth=420`, avg_drain=18req/s, pending_warmups=34. That drain rate won't catch up until scaled instances are warmed.
sana: hypothesis A: HPA acted, but warmup pipeline (kernel selection + quant init) is slow under cold start -> effective capacity delayed. Hypothesis B: specific model variant triggered heavier kernel path (longer warmup) + occasional OOM retries causing backpressure.
kevin: adding logs from scheduler controller: `scale request accepted but instance creation delayed by 230s` and cloud provider notifications showing GPU driver init failures for some instances.
liv (oncall): immediate mitigation options? can we divert new requests to dedicated fallback variant (smaller model) to reduce warmup?
matt: we have a compatible distill variant. We could promote routing rule to fallback tier for the next 30m. Manual change, low risk.
sana: also proposing to temporarily bump warmup concurrency for the warmup driver on that pool from 2->6 to reduce queue. risk: higher memory pressure during warmup.
tilly (infra): I can patch warmup concurrency and also force-recreate the stuck nodes (image pull flake). If we recreate, we might lose some pending warmup progress but nodes come online faster.
liv (oncall): do both: promote fallback routing + increase warmup concurrency. I'll coordinate with cust-success for comms. matt, sana you get the routing and warmup patch? tilly, please kick the recreate.
matt: routing change applied: `route: model-prod -> fallback-distill` with 30m TTL. Confirmed 09:33.
sana: warmup concurrency tweak applied to pool-gpu-3: `WARMUP_CONCURRENCY=6` 09:34.
tilly (infra): kicked recreate of 2 stuck nodes (node-az3-7 & node-az3-8). cloud shows terminate/start at 09:35.
kevin: after mitigations: 09:39 queue_depth=120, drain=42 req/s, pending_warmups=6. Latencies trending down.
liv (oncall): Good. keep monitoring. We need logs and timeline for RCA. Start collecting: HPA events, node lifecycle, warmup driver traces, kernel_warmup latencies, oom counts.
matt: grabbing HPA event history and sample controller logs. Pasting snapshot:
```
09:17: HPA observed cpu=60% target=50 -> desired=6
09:20: HPA scaled to 6 replicas (requested)
09:22: kubelet: PodPending nodeAffinity: no matching nodes
09:24: cloud: GPU driver init failed for new instances (timeout 90s)
09:26: node-ready events for 2/6
09:33: routing switch to fallback-distill applied
```
sana: warmup trace dump (sample):
```
warmup_trace: start=09:19:01 id=drv-7 stage=load_weights time=4300ms
warmup_trace: id=drv-7 stage=kernel_select time=8800ms
warmup_trace: id=drv-8 stage=kv_cache_init time=2100ms
```
kevin: OOMs correlated with nodes that had lower memory (misreported instance flavor) — cloud account had a partial mis-tag causing two spot instances to spin up with smaller memory profile. Raising an ops ticket for a provider-side mapping error.
liv (oncall): OK for in-thread timeline and hypotheses: - timeline: queue increase 09:18 -> HPA request 09:20 -> nodes start 09:23 -> nodes ready 09:26 -> routing fallback 09:33 -> stabilization 09:39. - hypotheses: warmup cold start latency + mis-provisioned node types + occasional OOMs causing retries/backpressure -> combined to create capacity shortfall.
matt: action items for RCA: (1) capture full warmup traces for all new instances, (2) cross-check cloud instance types for mismatch, (3) add early-detection metric: warmup_inflight > X should trigger temporary routing fallback automatically, (4) evaluate warmup concurrency safety.
sana: I can own 1 & 4. will run stress replay on staging to measure warmup concurrency effects.
tilly (infra): I'll continue to pursue provider mapping and add a guard in the autoscaler to verify instance hours/flavor before attaching to pool.
kevin: I'll open the provider ops ticket and attach the node metadata + image logs.
liv (oncall): Handoff if still hot? I'm staying on for 30m. If any of you pick up follow-ups, drop notes here. Also flag for post-incident: consider shorter HPA cool-down or pre-warm for expected daily spikes.
cust-success-bot: Notifying affected customers with ETA ~30-45m for full remediation.
matt: leaving notes for postmortem: include cost/benefit of autoscale warm pre-warm vs reserved buffer; collect metric shards for query patterns that caused heavy kernel paths.
sana: adding hypothesis tracker: [A] warmup latency (primary), [B] mis-provisioned instance type (secondary), [C] OOMs amplifying backpressure (tertiary). Will update with evidence.
liv (oncall): Great. Closing the live pager once metrics fully normalized. Current: latency back to baseline, queue depth stable. I'll file the incident ticket and assign postmortem owners. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
